references.text: Solomon's prayer to be able to judge righteously, which can be seen as a parallel to Herodias' daughter's request for John the Baptist's head, reflects the use of power and desires in leadership.

The story of Naboth's vineyard and how Queen Jezebel arranged Naboth's murder to fulfill King Ahab's desire shows how a person in power can manipulate situations to achieve their wishes, similar to Herodias' manipulation to obtain John the Baptist's head.
Daniel in the lion's den illustrates how Daniel was thrown into the lion's den because of the king's decree, which can be compared to John the Baptist being beheaded due to Herod's promise.
The story of Herod celebrating his birthday, where Herodias' daughter danced for him and asked for John the Baptist's head, directly recounts the event referred to in Matthew 14:8.
Luke's version of the event where Herod imprisoned John because of Herodias, his brother's wife, and John's criticism of their relationship, which led to the desire for his head.
Mark's detailed description of how Herodias' daughter asked for John the Baptist's head on a platter after being instructed by her mother, parallel to the event described in Matthew.
